record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)
record.original_question: Describe all triangular norms T, without assuming left-continuity, that satisfy T(x, 1 - T(1 - x, x)) = x for every x in [0,1]. This equation arises from requiring standard alpha-cuts of fuzzy sets to coincide with T-based alpha-cuts of the corresponding intuitionistic fuzzy sets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A triangular norm is a binary operation T : [0,1]×[0,1] → [0,1] that is commutative, associative, nondecreasing in each argument, and satisfies the boundary condition T(x,1) = x for every x ∈ [0,1]. Without imposing left-continuity (or any continuity assumption) on T, determine all triangular norms T such that
    T(x, 1 − T(1 − x, x)) = x
holds for every x ∈ [0,1]. Equivalently, give a complete characterization of the class of triangular norms satisfying this identity.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for the specific functional equation T(x, 1 − T(1 − x, x)) = x on triangular norms did not return any paper providing a full characterization without left-continuity. General references on t-norms (Klement–Mesiar–Pap and others) do not appear to address this identity directly, so the current status could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: Triangular norm - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: General survey of triangular norms and their characterizations; no mention of the specific equation T(x,1-T(1-x,x))=x.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references on t-norms do not discuss this particular functional equation.

status_evidence.title: Triangular norms. Position paper I
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of analytic and algebraic properties of t-norms without addressing the equation in question.
status_evidence.claim: No characterization of the equation appears in foundational t-norm surveys.
